BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF SCAFFOLD DESIGN

This document describes the structural design of a cantilever scaffold required for maintenance of in-let piping to A-3302 for equipment tag A-3302 under work order 10086944 at Jetty 1 / B. The scaffold envelope is 7.2m x 3.5m x 3m (length x width x height) and is configured with standards, ledgers, transoms, bracing, platforms, access, and support/tie arrangements as indicated on the approved drawing.

SAFE WORKING LOAD (SWL): 1.5 kN/m²

Note: This is a category 1 engineered scaffold. Scaffold shall be inspected and approved for use by assurance engineer before tagging for use.

GENERAL NOTE
BS EN 12811-1, 4.2.1.2 Scaffold materials are in accordance with BS EN 12811 with minimum design strength of 210 N/mm². This design calculation was carried out in accordance with the limit states design method stipulated in EN 1993-1-1:2005 (Eurocode 3 - Design of Steel Structures).
Material Properties

48.3 mm outside diameter x 3.6 mm thick steel tube was defined by STAAD.Pro Connect Edition V22 section tables (British) and assigned to all scaffold members as section PIP483.6.

Modelling Philosophy
BS EN 12811-1, 4.2.1.2 A 3-D model was analysed using STAAD.Pro CONNECT Edition (V22) in compliance with EN 1993-1-1:2005. Base supports are modelled as pinned with lateral spring stiffness representing frictional restraint (KFX/KFZ = 13.574 kN). Base supports are modelled as elastic spring supports, restrained laterally in both horizontal directions with rotational degrees of freedom released, representing flexible ground contact conditions at each standard foot. See Appendix A for model views.
LOAD CASES

Load diagrams are shown in Appendix B.

Dead Load / Self-weight Self-weight of structural elements computed by STAAD.Pro with steel density 76.8195 kN/m³, with a 10% allowance for fittings and couplers (selfweight factor = 1.1).
Live Load on Platforms
BS EN 12811-1 Platform live loading was applied to the scaffold working platforms as member UDLs in the STAAD model. The platform load intensity is multiplied by the tributary width to obtain the line load applied to platform supporting members. (LC 2).

Member Load = Service Load x Tributary Width. Edge members take half the adjacent bay width; interior members take half the bay width from each side.
Governing platform live load intensity used for SWL = 1.5 kN/m².
Total applied platform live load = 12.6 kN.
Handrail Load
Handrail loads were applied where required by the scaffold configuration and modelled independently in the global X and Z directions.

Handrail Load (HLZ) = 1.44 kN (member UDL 0.15 kN/m)

CONCLUSION
The structural analysis and design of the cantilever scaffold confirms the structure is adequate for its intended purpose. All member utilization ratios are below unity (maximum UC = 0.579 at Member 45). Vertical and horizontal deflections are within their respective allowable limits of L/100 = 24.0mm and L/200 = 8.5mm. All scaffold tube coupler connections are adequate for the applied axial loads.
RECOMMENDATIONS
The scaffold shall be inspected by a competent Scaffold Inspector after erection to confirm conformity with the design specification and approved working drawings before use. All erection work shall comply with the design intent and material specification. Any proposed change to the design requires a re-design and the Scaffold Engineer shall be duly informed.
INSTALLATION NOTES
  1. The scaffold working drawings and purpose of the scaffold must be reviewed and discussed by all personnel involved prior to execution.
  2. Confirm that the cantilever scaffold configuration matches the approved drawing and is suitable for maintenance of in-let piping to A-3302.
  3. The work vicinity must be barricaded and appropriate signage placed at all access points.
  4. All scaffolders must wear complete PPE in accordance with NLNG work-at-height regulations.
  5. A valid work permit must be obtained, discussed, and signed before erection commences.
  6. Scaffold erection must be carried out in strict accordance with NASC guidance and site safety procedures.
  7. Install and secure cantilever support members, needles, anchors, ties, and back-span restraints exactly as shown on the approved drawing before building the working platform.
  8. Build the scaffold frame to the approved envelope of 7.2m x 3.5m x 3.0m, checking level, plumb, and cantilever projection at each lift.
  9. Install bracing, ledgers, transoms, platform boards, guardrails, and toe boards progressively, maintaining all specified ties and restraints.
  10. Install mid-level horizontal ledgers and transoms at 2.0m height in accordance with the working drawing.
  11. Install mid-level horizontal ledgers and transoms at 2.5m height in accordance with the working drawing.
  12. Install all plan, face, and longitudinal bracing shown on the approved drawing to provide sway resistance in both principal directions.
  13. Install platform boards, guardrails, mid-rails, toe boards, access arrangements, and any handrail load-resisting members required by the design.
  14. Tighten and torque-check all load-bearing couplers and support connections before the scaffold is released for inspection.
  15. Gravlock or box-tie the scaffold structure to the existing structure at all indicated tie points at 0.3m and 2.0m height as shown on the working drawing.
  16. The scaffold structure must be inspected and tagged by a competent advance scaffold inspector after erection and before use.
  17. The safe working load (SWL) stated on the design report must not be exceeded at any time during operations.
  18. All modifications made after erection must be carried out by a competent scaffold team with the approval of the scaffold engineer. End-user or third-party modification of this scaffold structure is strictly prohibited.
  19. For dismantling, perform the erection steps in reverse order.

APPENDIX E - TOTAL RESTRAINT DEMAND AT TIE SUPPORTS
Total Restraint Demand at Tie Supports (X and Z)
Definition: Total Restraint Demand = Sum |FX| and Sum |FZ| at the relevant support/tie nodes, with no directional cancellation. Resultant H(abs) = sqrt((Sum |FX|)² + (Sum |FZ|)²). This metric is used separately for cumulative tie/restraint demand review because every restraint force contribution is counted by magnitude. It is not combined with, averaged with, or substituted for the Net Global Reaction on the parent structure. Relevant tie nodes: 7, 8, 19, 20, 21, 22, 27.
